newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S BANK HANDLOWY EUROBOND AT UP TO $200 MLN.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S BANK HANDLOWY EUROBOND AT UP TO $200 MLN.

text.p: Poland's Bank Handlowy SA plans to issue up to $200 million of its dollar eurobond to be led by JP Morgan and scheduled for early in the second quarter of this year, a senior Handlowy official said on Wednesday.
On Tuesday Handlowy announced it had mandated JP Morgan to lead an issue of likely three or five-year bonds, which would take place early in the second quarter, but gave no details.
"This will be (a eurobond) issue of up to $200 million," Wlodzimierz Kasprzak, a department director at Handlowy, told Reuters.
He added that the issue would not be smaller than $100 million.
Kasprzak said the proceeds from the issue would be used for the operational activities of the bank and that its size would be tailored to the the bank's specific needs.
He said Handlowy would soon announce further details of the issue including its pricing range.

Handlowy, Poland's leading commercial bank, is earmarked for privatisation this year with about 30 percent of shares set aside for an initial public offering in June. The bank also plans to offer 30 percent of shares to a group of international financial institutions.
In 1996 Handlowy issued Poland's first-ever corporate $100 million eurobond and was awarded a Baa3 rating by Moody's.
